magna_mater_arrives_204.summary: The black meteorite of Cybele from Pessinus, received at Ostia by P. Scipio Nasica, was passed hand to hand by the leading matrons to the city and placed in the Temple of Victoria on the Palatine on 12 April, a day made a festival with gifts, a lectisternium and the first games, the Megalesia.

gallic_entry_porta_collina.summary: Shortly after the Allia (the next day in Livy, the third day in Plutarch) the Gauls found the Colline Gate open and the walls unguarded. They marched down to the Forum, where the old ex-magistrates sat waiting in their robes of office in the atria of their houses.
gallic_entry_porta_collina.note: Livy says the Gauls entered 'porta Collina'. The Servian wall in stone postdates the sack; gate position is that of the later Porta Collina. Year is Varronian (390); Polybius (1.6.1-2) synchronises the sack with the Peace of Antalcidas and Dionysius' siege of Rhegium, i.e. 387/386 BC, the date most historians accept.

dedication_capitoline_temple_509.note: 509 is the Varronian year of the first consuls; Polybius (3.22.1) dates them 28 years before Xerxes' crossing, i.e. 508/507 BC.

theatre_marcellus_dedication_13.note: Dio puts the dedication in 13 BC; Pliny (NH 8.65) dates it, with the tame tiger, to 4 May 11 BC (consuls Tubero and Fabius Maximus).

forum_augustus_dedication_2.note: The day is disputed: Ovid (Fasti 5.545-598) gives 12 May, Dio (60.5.3) has the games of Mars Ultor on 1 August; 1 August follows the latter view.

fortuna_redux_altar_19.note: 12 October 19 BC is the day of Augustus' return, when the altar was voted (constituta) and the feriae created; the altar was dedicated on 15 December 19 BC (Fasti Amiternini).

temple_ceres_liber_libera_493.note: Exact site not excavated; placed from the ancient descriptions near the carceres. No ancient source states the dedication day; 19 April assumes it fell on the Cerialia.

october_horse_46.note: Dio does not say the soldiers were killed at the October Horse festival, only that they were sacrificed in the Campus Martius by the pontiffs and the flamen of Mars during Caesar's triumphal celebrations; the link and the 15 October date are modern inferences.

argei_pons_sublicius.summary: In mid-May (14 May in Ovid's calendar, the Ides in Dionysius) the Vestals threw 27 rush puppets in human shape from the wooden Pons Sublicius into the Tiber, a rite whose meaning puzzled Ovid and his contemporaries.

catana_sundial_rostra_263.summary: M'. Valerius Messalla brought a sundial from captured Catana and set it on a column beside the Rostra. Its lines, drawn for Catana, did not match the hours at Rome, but Romans told the time by it for 99 years.

fire_salinae_carmentalis_213.summary: A fire burned for two nights and a day, levelling everything between the salt stores and the Porta Carmentalis, including the Aequimaelium, the Vicus Iugarius and the temples of Fortuna and Mater Matuta, and spread widely outside the gate, where the temple of Spes also had to be rebuilt.

secular_games_tarentum_17.summary: On the night of 31 May Augustus sacrificed nine ewes and nine she-goats to the Moirai on altars by the Tiber at the Tarentum, followed by stage plays on a stage with no theatre and no seats; Augustus alone made the night sacrifices, while Agrippa joined him for the daytime sacrifices on the Capitol.
secular_games_tarentum_17.note: The inscribed Acta were found in 1890 near the Tiber by Corso Vittorio Emanuele, close to the Tarentum. Marker on the underground altar of Dis and Proserpina found in 1886-87.

asellio_killed_castor_89.note: Valerius Maximus (9.7.4) places the sacrifice before the Temple of Concord; Appian (BC 1.54) says he was sacrificing to Castor and Pollux in the Forum.
